faqs.a: The tool extracts the text of both PDFs and runs a longest-common-subsequence diff over their lines — the same core idea behind code diff tools, applied to document text.
Tables and images have no text lines to compare, so they are skipped. If the table's text is selectable in the PDF, its words still appear in the line stream.
faqs.q: Can it compare tables or images?

faqs.a: Turn on the whitespace option (default). It collapses extra spaces before comparing, so re-wrapped lines do not show as changes.
faqs.q: The files only differ in spacing. Can I ignore that?

faqs.a: Yes — up to 1,200 lines per document are compared, which covers contracts, reports and books chapters comfortably.

compare-pdf.formula:
dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j+1] + 1            if lineA[i] = lineB[j]
dp[i][j] = max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1])  otherwise

Walk the table from the top-left: equal lines are “unchanged”, otherwise follow the larger neighbor — down means a removed line, right means an added line.
Example: A=[“Total: 500”], B=[“Total: 650”] → 1 removed + 1 added, 0 unchanged for that line.
howTo: Keep whitespace-insensitive mode on to ignore formatting noise.
Click compare and wait for both texts to be extracted.
Read the side-by-side diff: red lines were removed, green lines were added.
keyFacts: Both PDFs are converted to text with pdf.js, then compared line by line with an LCS diff.
The result is a two-column table: original on the left, revised on the right.
Removed lines are highlighted red, added lines green, unchanged lines stay neutral.
Summary counts show unchanged, removed and added lines at a glance.
Whitespace collapsing is optional; up to 1,200 lines per document are compared.

limitations: Only text is compared — images, charts and layout changes are invisible to the diff.
Scanned PDFs have no text layer, so they cannot be compared.
Very large PDFs (100+ pages) can be slow to process and may use significant browser memory.
Password-protected PDFs that need a password prompt cannot be read.

compare-pdf.workedExample:
Invoice v1 lines: [“Invoice #101”, “Total: 500”, “Thanks”].
Invoice v2 lines: [“Invoice #101”, “Total: 650”, “Thanks”].
LCS matches lines 1 and 3 as unchanged.
Line 2 differs → 1 removed (“Total: 500”) + 1 added (“Total: 650”).
Summary: unchanged 2, removed 1, added 1 — the only change is the total, 500 → 650.
